newsitem.title: USA: Baxter - Immuno deal gets final U.S.approval.
newsitem.headline: Baxter - Immuno deal gets final U.S.approval.

text.p: The U.S. government gave final approval Friday for Baxter International Inc to buy Immuno International AG, creating the world's largest blood products manufacturer.

On December 19 the Federal Trade Commission gave conditional clearance for the deal but required Baxter to sell off its Autoplex product within four months to prevent a monopoloy in products needed by hemophiliacs in the U.S.
A spokeswoman for Baxter, headquartered in Deerfield, Ill., said today the firm had taken steps to sell off Autoplex and had submitted paperwork to the government for approval.
Baxter also has said it will license Immuno's "fibrin sealant," a product used to stop bleeding during surgery or after a traumatic injury and to promote the healing of wounds.
Baxter and Immuno, based in Zalikon, Switzerland, are among a very few companies that manufacture fibrin sealant, which the U.S. government estimates to be a $400 million annual business in the U.S.
